title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
why: Locates unmet multi-agent task conditions and repairs actions or graph dependencies while retaining previously validated contributions.
note: 2026 preprint; evaluated across 30 applications and six MAS frameworks. Reported task accuracy is not external transaction integrity.

title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution
why: Plans safe continuation after ambiguous tool outcomes using publicly supported effect states, provider contracts and independent replay certificates.
note: 2026 preprint; finite assignments and local-model comparisons. Certificates depend on declared provider capabilities; no general exactly-once guarantee.

title: Verify--Backtrack Loop: Structured Precondition Recovery for Long-Horizon Language Agents
why: Uses goal-stack verification and typed failure attribution to trigger explicit retry, subgoal updates or backtracking after unmet prerequisites.
note: 2026 preprint; AppWorld, ALFWorld and ScienceWorld experiments. Backtracking is an agent planning-state operation, not arbitrary external rollback.

title: AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers
why: Benchmarks web-agent recovery from blocked links, authorization walls and rate limits while preserving the original authorized goal.
note: 2026 preprint; sandbox and real-website replay. Alternative resources must remain legitimate and policy-compliant; not generic transaction rollback.

title: ReplayRCA: Measuring Post-hoc Diagnosis and Live Oversight of Agent Failures by Counterfactual Replay
why: Restores failed LLM agent execution to the selected step and tests whether a proposed corrected action improves outcome against a placebo replay.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; deterministic OpsWorld evaluations and single-step intervention. Causal repair is measured against placebo, not external-world rollback.

title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
why: Tests whether candidate repairs selected by a different evaluator improve the deployed agent's own rollouts.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; tested on ALFWorld and WebShop. Reported 7B-versus-14B repair-ranking losses depend on the evaluator/executor pairing.

title: Monitor Accuracy Isn't the Answer: A Decision-Value Framework for Evaluating AI Agent Restart Monitors
why: Evaluates restart-versus-continue decisions based on replacement opportunity, remaining budget and certification rather than monitor accuracy alone.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 194 model executions on 19 SymPy SWE-bench Verified issues, with no certified positive result in 103 reported live comparisons; simple independent restart assumptions.

title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Analyzes natural self-recovery and predicts when external intervention is necessary.
note: Very recent preprint.

title: AndroidFlux: Evaluating and Reward Modeling Failure Recovery Capabilities in Mobile Use Multimodal Agents
why: Replays AndroidWorld device states at controlled error checkpoints to isolate mobile-agent recovery from clean-task competence.
note: 2026 preprint; checkpoints and offline RL evaluation use a controlled mobile environment, not arbitrary persistent external side effects.

title: Async-RBench: Benchmarking Asynchronous Task Execution in LLM Agents
why: Replays delayed stale duplicate and failed subagent results under explicit preserve update and re-verification contracts.
note: 2026 preprint; 200 executable tasks and nine evaluated agents; Dynamic Replanning Score is separate from end-task success.

title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
why: MCP-Injector reproduces protocol-aware permanent transient and intermittent tool faults using ecosystem incident evidence.
note: 2026 arXiv paper reports NeurIPS 2026 poster acceptance; tested two gpt-oss model sizes and three agent stacks; scale claim is limited to those comparisons.

title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
why: Measures whether agents seek omitted safety-critical facts before taking otherwise dangerous tool actions.
note: 2026 preprint; 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs. Evidence acquisition is not restoration of external state.

title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
why: Examines whether recovering workflows still have authority to dispatch reconcile or retry an uncertain external effect.
note: 2026 preprint; 336 finite histories across native LangGraph and Temporal hosts; ancillary result files are linked from arXiv; no unrestricted production authorization guarantee.

title: Don't Forget What You Just Learned: Self-Directed Repair Turns Agent Mistakes Into Lasting Lessons
why: Turns failed agent trajectories into persistent low-rank lesson adapters routed to related future tasks.
note: 2026 preprint; GAIA Claw-Eval and Terminal-Bench 2.1 results are author-reported. Transfer and repeated-error reduction do not demonstrate safe restoration of external effects.

title: Back Up Before You Regret: Measuring Backup Awareness and Automating Backup in Coding Agents
why: Studies preventive backup and the BackUpper layer for coding agent actions.
note: Does not imply external effects are reversible.

title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
why: Benchmarks recognition and repair of inherited desktop errors over persistent workflows.
note: Paper reports 2250 test states.

title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
why: Introduces ReTrace and transition-consistent recovery scoring for computer-use agents restoring GUI state after controlled mistakes.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; goal-oriented action replay and injected GUI errors, not proof of remote system transaction rollback.

title: RITE: Evaluating End-to-End Resilience to Silent Tool Errors in E-Commerce Agentic Systems
why: Contrasts plausible incorrect tool values with correct values and explicit failures to measure recognition verification and end-task recovery.
note: 2026 preprint; 501 instances from 167 matched units and nine e-commerce workflows; domain-specific simulated tool behavior.

title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
why: Learns when and how to amend in-progress multi-agent trajectories from execution-verified correction pairs.
note: 2026 preprint; author-reported repair results across selected frameworks and benchmarks, not independent external-effect verification.

title: How GUI Agents Fail: GraceBench for Execution Stability Diagnosis
why: Measures recovery ability along with deviation, loops and stagnation in GUI-agent traces using graph-aligned UI transitions.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 169 tasks in ten apps and trajectory stability scores; recovery ability is a metric, not automated environment repair.

title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
why: Releases perturbation-grounded reflection skills and training recipes for recovering from noisy tools and user corrections.
note: 2026 work-in-progress preprint; code model weights and data are released; training/benchmark robustness is not proof of real external effect repair.

title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
why: BELIEFWEAVER retains evidence across failing attempts and checkpoints and uses belief updates plus prospective world modeling to guide repair.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; three terminal-agent benchmarks with author-reported gains; persistent reasoning state does not establish side-effect integrity.

title: TRAP: Tool-result Replay Attack for Probing Misbinding in LLM Agents
why: Measures stale and cross-context replay of genuine tool results during agent recovery and evaluates contextual binding defenses.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; ReplayBench scenarios use controlled result replay and defenses, not claims of universal security.

title: When Messages Go Wrong: Understanding Communication Faults in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
why: Injects message loss delays and partial content and measures propagation and evidence recovery across multi-agent topologies.
note: 2026 preprint; more than 29,000 author-reported executions across 100 tasks; recovery depends on surviving independent evidence paths.

title: RetryBench: Separating Retry Permission from Recovery Outcomes in GPT Tool Use
why: Separately measures unsupported dispatch after timed-out tool calls and eventual outcome to distinguish false retry permission from actual recovery.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint revised October 22; four purposive tasks, model endpoint comparisons and one recovery decision; does not certify episode-level safety.

title: How Do Hardware Faults Manifest Differently in LLM Agents?
why: Injects random model-weight faults across agent runs to distinguish natural correction costly recovery silent errors and security deviations.
note: 2026 preprint; 6814 author-reported executions with sampled two-bit faults across three benchmarks. Studies resilience and spontaneous recovery; does not provide a recovery algorithm.

title: SSCBench: Evaluating the Evidential Validity of Fault-Injection Tests for Tool-Using LLM Agents
why: Checks whether counterevidence was available before an agent first relied on an injected false assertion.
note: 2026 preprint; 1,191 faulted executions in two tau-bench environments; measures evidential conditions, not repaired outcomes.

title: Loud Failures, Quiet Failures: Fault Detection and Recovery in Tool-Using Language Model Agents
why: Separately tracks noticing faulty tools replanning retry loops and task recovery for explicit versus silent errors.
note: 2026 preprint; 1,920 trials across 24 tasks; stochastic clean-run variation complicates fault-attributed recovery comparisons.

title: StateWise: Diagnosing and Repairing Persistent Operational State Before Agent Actions
why: Diagnoses invalid persistent agent records using counterfactual replanning and evidence checks, repairs records and verifies subsequent proposed actions.
note: 2026 preprint; 150 executable coding-agent cases. Pre-action state repair is not proof of remote effect reversal.

title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
why: Measures conditional recovery separately from nominal task competence under phased enterprise write failures.
note: Preprint; 2,880 paired lost-acknowledgment trials are author-reported. Not evidence of production exactly-once guarantees.

title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
why: Conditionally retrieves failure lessons and verifies repaired execution.
note: Check code release state.

title: DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents
why: Uses event-dependency and failure-propagation graphs to localize decisive errors and feed targeted improvements into skill evolution.
note: 2026 preprint; Who-and-When and multimodal attribution plus Trace2Skill gains are author-reported. Step diagnosis is not itself a verified repair.

title: Recova: Agent-Guided Failure Recovery for Autonomous Robotic Manipulation
why: Discovers and trains executable robot recovery skills in digital twins then verifies scene restoration during real-robot rollouts.
note: 2026 preprint; real-robot and simulation results are author-reported. Physical restoration is task and scene dependent and not a software transaction guarantee.

title: Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover
why: Tests revalidation and validated rollback when self-editing agents retain unsafe executable revisions.
note: 2026 preprint; controlled authorization testbed; safety transfer to unrestricted deployment unproven.

title: AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Links evidence-grounded failure diagnosis to bounded recovery proposals and controlled reruns.
note: EMNLP 2026 System Demonstrations; GAIA rerun results are author-reported and need a controlled environment.

title: AgentRx: Diagnosing AI Agent Failures from Execution Trajectories
why: Synthesizes per-step constraints and auditable violation logs to localize critical failure steps.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; 170 annotated trajectories in final ACL version (earlier Microsoft materials mention 115); diagnosis only.

title: From Credit Assignment to Repair: A Leakage-Controlled Diagnostic Study of Tool-Using Agents
why: Tests whether failure localization causes useful selective tool-agent repair and reports a reproducible negative result for its selected intervention gate.
note: REALM 2026 workshop; on tested tau2-bench tasks interventions rarely changed trajectories and did not improve binary reward. Negative result, not a recovery solution.

title: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
why: Inspects paired screenshots and actions for causal GUI errors and conditions re-execution on structured diagnosis.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; CUAErrorBench has 204 annotated failures; rerollout results depend on controlled restart settings.

title: Finding Where the Buck Stops: An Automated Failure Attribution-Based Reflection Framework for Multi-Agent Collaboration
why: DoCtOR targets reflection and correction at the decisive error agent and step instead of the entire team.
note: EMNLP 2026; reported improvements on question answering and web tasks, not generic multi-service rollback.

title: EDGE: Error Dependency Graph-Guided Multi-Error Attribution in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
why: Builds error-dependency graphs and validates causal subsets via counterfactual rollout for multi-error attribution in LLM multi-agent failures.
note: Findings of EMNLP 2026; TRAIL and MAST attribution evaluations, not independently demonstrated end-to-end repair or external-state verification.

title: HiP-LR: Hierarchical Planning with Localized Failure Recovery for Long-Horizon Multi-Robot Tasks
why: Localizes replanning to affected groups after runtime faults so unaffected LLM-coordinated robot agents can continue.
note: Findings of EMNLP 2026; RECAP-THOR failure-injection tests in a specialized multi-robot environment.

title: What Drives Recovery in Agentic Text-to-Cypher? LAST-CQ: An LLM Agent Self-Refinement Framework
why: Uses live-database counterfactuals to separate the benefit of failure-triggered retries from elaborate feedback or extra sampling.
note: REALM at EMNLP 2026 workshop; 2471 database queries and six backbones. Execution-grounded query correction is domain-specific and not a remote-write recovery guarantee.

title: Causal Decomposition of LLM Agent Failure via Oracle-State Intervention
why: Tests whether replacing polluted context with oracle state actually rescues failed long-horizon agents.
note: REALM 2026 workshop; under 10% recovered after context replacement in stated WebArena default settings.

title: ParaRecover: A Process-Level Benchmark for Error Localization and Recovery in Parallel Tool-Use Agents
why: Evaluates cascading failure diagnosis and replanning across dependent parallel tool-call branches.
note: EMNLP 2026; 10,626 instances and 14 error types are author-reported; no global transaction guarantees.

title: PRFC: Learning Progressive Recovery from Function Calling Errors for Tool-Using LLMs
why: Trains successive corrective tool calls with progress-aware rewards after observed function-calling failures.
note: Findings of EMNLP 2026; multi-turn BFCL-v3 and three single-step tool tasks; improved call recovery does not certify external effects.

title: RecoverAgent: Intent-Preserving Recovery from Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-using LLM Agents
why: Rewrites unsafe injected intermediate responses to resume permitted user goals after threat detection.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; tested on prompt-injection benchmarks. Safe continuation still requires tool outcome checks.

title: RESKILL: Explicit Failure Attribution and Structured Repair for Interactive Language Agents
why: Keeps structured failure hypotheses and retest feedback to choose and revise agent skill repairs.
note: EMNLP 2026; demonstrated on ALFWorld and TextCraft under fixed repair budgets, not real external writes.

title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents
why: RetryRealistic provides sandboxed real file SQLite and HTTP faults with correct fabricated and honest-failure outcome labels.
note: NeurIPS 2026 workshop paper per author and released code; 30 tasks and nine fault types. The monitor cannot engage on never-signaled silent faults; OpenReview landing page may require login.

title: ToolMisuseBench: An Offline Deterministic Benchmark for Tool Misuse and Recovery in Agentic Systems
why: Measures deterministic fault-conditioned recovery with typed recoverability and output-grounded scoring.
note: REALM 2026 workshop; seed-42 release includes 1,200 public-test tasks; offline evaluation.

title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
why: Separates initially wrong decisions from resolved errors and terminally relevant causal failures in long traces.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; TrajErrBench reports 486 annotated failed trajectories; step localization is not rollback.

title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training
why: Pairs error diagnoses with candidate corrections and matched replay from common checkpoints when available.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 50228 pairs and 3062 matched reruns are author-reported; resettable environments only.

title: When Harnesses Lose the Signal: Causal Evaluation of Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Compares paired continuations with versus without a harness recovery operation to measure both rescued and harmed trajectories.
note: 2026 preprint; ALFWorld and one tested model setting, not a cross-domain guarantee of intervention value.

title: Fault-Tolerant Budget Conservation in Distributed Multi-Agent Delegation
why: Preserves delegated agent resource budgets under crash, duplicate delivery, partition and late commit through effect reservations and reconciled settlement.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; proofs and bounded TLA+ checks plus crash-injected SQLite tests require explicit mediation and gateway assumptions.

title: Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models
why: Benchmarks unsupported completion claims after failed tool observations and evaluates an evidence-structured status response.
note: 2026 preprint; author-reported 3,600 responses in synthetic blocked-task cases; reporting accuracy does not equal actual task recovery.

title: Same Winners, Different Success Rates: Evaluating How LLM Agents Recover from Failures
why: Shows why agreement on the best checkpoint action can hide uniformly poor absolute recovery success.
note: 2026 preprint; recommends reporting all-zero fraction and pooled or held-out success alongside agreement.

title: Beyond Approved Actions: Runtime Validation of Persistent Outcomes in Agent Workflows
why: EffectMatch checks observed persistent changes against approved effects before committing or allowing downstream execution.
note: 2026 preprint; guarantees depend on a controlled execution boundary and accurate observation of effects.

title: Where Does Exactly-Once Live? Model, Harness, and Tool-Contract Effects on Duplicate Side Effects in LLM Agents
why: LIMBO injects late commits, duplicate delivery and partial batches; effect ledgers expose unsafe retries.
note: Preprint; 25,930 author-reported episodes. Tool-level idempotency contracts can be necessary where read-back cannot resolve in-flight writes.

title: MeshHeal: Two-Timescale Self-Healing for Gray Failures in Decentralized LLM Agent Networks
why: Explores escalation and verification during containment and reintegration of degraded agents.

title: Self-Healing Harness for Runtime Oversight of Agent Self-Modification
why: Gates persistent agent self-modifications on demonstrated improvement without unacceptable regressions.

title: Collective Loss of Control in LLM Agent Systems: An Epidemic Account of Mutation, Contagion, and Recovery
why: Analyzes how erroneous agent behaviors spread across multi-agent systems and recover.

title: Rollback the World, Keep the Reflection: Rollback-Induced Reflection for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
why: Couples controlled environment rollback with retained knowledge from the failed trajectory to guide subsequent agent execution.
note: 2026 preprint; evaluated in resettable interactive environments, not arbitrary third-party irreversible effects.

title: Locating Hidden Failures Makes Long-Horizon Agents More Reliable
why: Traverse labels mistakes and Scout predicts first-error locations.
note: Authors report 2518 trajectories and 6967 mistakes.

title: When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail: Anomalies at the Agent-Tool Boundary
why: Classifies external-effect anomalies that can survive tool success and derives reconciliation and transaction contract requirements at the agent-tool boundary.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; effect-history model and MCP annotation audit over 98,291 tools, not an implemented general recovery engine.

title: Engineering Reliable Commit Gates for Agentic AI: Cost-Aware Verification Portfolios under Common-Mode Data Failures
why: Tests independent evidence, commit guards, concurrent writes and lost responses to distinguish verification from effect safety.
note: 2026 preprint; controlled faults plus bounded HTTP/SQLite study. Generalization across unseen fault families is limited.

title: REVISE: Validity-Guided Recovery for Online Revisions in Agent Workflows
why: Uses workflow dependency provenance to retain still-valid work and recompute only the portions invalidated by a live revision.
note: 2026 preprint; 300 evaluated revision/commit cases on structured DAG workflows. Addresses changing instructions and stale work rather than all runtime failures.

title: Agent Error Simulator: Fault Injection for Testing Recovery in Agentic Workflows
why: Declarative proxy fault injection probes format logic and tool failures across planner worker and aggregator roles.
note: IEEE eScience 2026; results from an example hierarchical workflow and HPC-centric setup, not broad agent robustness.

title: Localizing Emergent Failures in Agentic AI: Recovering Minimal Repair Families via Counterfactual Replay
why: Uses graph-constrained counterfactual replay to test combined repair interventions.

title: Safe to Resume? Breaking Execution Continuity of Agent Execution via Rollback
why: Studies insecure checkpoint/rollback across agent frameworks including stale dependencies, nondeterministic replay, and unrecorded external effects.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; examined five framework designs and reported three end-to-end attack demonstrations; a security diagnosis study, not a general-purpose repair guarantee.

title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
why: Aligns agent-context and environment-state checkpoints for resumable execution.

title: Retry, Switch, or Abstain? Learning Strategy-Aware Tool-Use Policies via Controlled Error Injection
why: BENCH2ROBUST distinguishes retry switching tools and safe stopping under controlled failure solvability.
note: 2026 preprint; results reflect tested retail/tool benchmarks and do not guarantee real-world effect reversal.

title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction
why: Profiles failure classes and selects admissible recovery interventions before test-time agent self-correction.
note: 2026 preprint; task-family profiling and frozen recovery policies; validity beyond evaluated environments remains unproven.

title: From Faulty Memories to Corrected Actions: Dependency-Guided Rollback Repair for Memory-Augmented Agents
why: Tracks faulty memories through dependent actions, repairs affected persistent state and selectively replays work while preserving unaffected records.
note: 2026 preprint revised October; controlled and trajectory-derived tests; residual recurrence observed after selective replay.

title: When Agentic Executions Fail: Detecting and Localizing Runtime Faults from Telemetry
why: AgentChaosBench injects MCP A2A guardrail and tool faults and evaluates fault localization from aligned execution traces.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 275 traces (250 faulty and 25 control); measures diagnosis, not verified task recovery.

title: Fail-Fast, Restart-Smart: Early Failure Prediction and Restart for SWE Agentic Tasks
why: Uses prefix-only early-failure monitoring and a fresh same-policy restart that can selectively reuse the interrupted code diff.
note: 2026 preprint; SWE-bench Verified reported token savings and recovery gains depend on chosen false-positive rate and coding-agent policies. A diff overlay is not universal side-effect rollback.

title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures
why: Combines step telemetry and deterministic verification with repair experiments.

title: Verified Tool Calls Improve LLM Agent Reliability Under Non-Atomic Failures
why: Studies postcondition checking verify-before-retry and idempotency keys under non-atomic simulated tool calls.
note: 2026 preprint; simulated faults only. Read-back alone cannot resolve all late or in-flight commits.

title: MemTX: Transactional Belief Commit for Stateful Agent Memory
why: Stages evidence-backed shared-memory writes and triggers cascading repair after a belief is retracted.
note: 2026 preprint; protocol invariants and tested environments do not imply universal compensation of irreversible actions.

title: AgentCheck: A Reproduce-Intervene-Mitigate Workbench for LLM Agents over MCP
why: Reproduces MCP tool faults and reruns agents under matched failures to test whether specific mitigations actually recover outcomes.
note: 2026 preprint; twelve injected fault types and five tested agents. Interpretive labels partly use LLM judgment; not broad production validation.

title: Repair the Core, Not the Symptom: Planning-Graph Repair for Long-Horizon Agents
why: Repairs a causally implicated core of a failed agent planning graph instead of changing one symptom or rerunning the whole graph.
note: 2026 preprint revised October; planning-graph study with evaluated controlled settings, not external-effect compensation.

title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
why: Introduces incident detection containment recovery and future guardrail synthesis inside agent execution.
note: ICML 2026; author-reported incident remediation results from three evaluated agent types, not independent production certification.

title: Robust Tool Use via Fission-GRPO: Learning to Recover from Execution Errors
why: Turns execution errors into on-policy training examples and resampled correction rollouts for multi-turn tool-call recovery.
note: ACL 2026 long paper; recovery rates are benchmark-specific; training benefit is not transaction-safe live replay.

title: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents
why: Introduces GUI-RobustEval with executable wrong-action recovery cases and RoTS recovery-trajectory synthesis.
note: ICML 2026; 1,216 test cases are author-reported. Controlled GUI evaluation is not arbitrary remote rollback.

title: Failure makes the agent stronger: Enhancing Accuracy through Structured Reflection for Reliable Tool Interactions
why: Benchmarks and trains explicit error diagnosis followed by an executable corrected tool call in failed multi-turn tool use.
note: Findings of ACL 2026; evaluated on BFCL v3 and Tool-Reflection-Bench; code release is not established by the proceedings text.

title: Seeing the Whole Elephant: A Benchmark for Failure Attribution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
why: Tests failure attribution under full agent inputs and metadata instead of output-only traces with reproducible environments.
note: ACL 2026 long paper; full observability improves attribution in tested systems. Attribution alone does not establish successful corrective execution.

title: Mnemosyne: Agentic Transaction Processing for Validating and Repairing AI-generated Workflows
why: Uses deterministic admission, persistent transition logs, dependency-safe compensation and bounded reactive repair for proposed workflow changes.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint revised August; stated correctness holds relative to specified executable constraints and adapters, not all external systems.

title: Beyond Function Calling: Benchmarking Tool-Using Agents under Tool-Environment Unreliability
why: Provides deterministic multi-step tasks with recoverable tool hazards and scores whether retry, fallback or verification succeeds.
note: 2026 preprint; seeded benchmark with constructed recovery paths, not necessarily real-world provider fault contracts.

title: Cordon: Semantic Transactions for Tool-Using LLM Agents
why: Stages agent tool effects in task-scoped semantic transactions with reversible shadow state, validation and recovery metadata.
note: 2026 preprint; staged effects and adapter boundaries only, not universal atomicity for all external systems.

title: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
why: Uses branch-level rollback and correction for resettable training-time web agents.
note: Resettable environment only.

title: REFLECT: Intervention-Supported Error Attribution for Silent Failures in LLM Agent Traces
why: Tests suspected silent agent errors with targeted patch-and-replay interventions before confirming causal attribution.
note: 2026 preprint; measures localization quality rather than end-to-end task or external-state recovery.

title: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents: Diagnosing and Repairing Harness Flaws
why: Maps failed agent traces to faulty runtime-harness components and applies scoped patches with regression-aware validation.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint revised July; repairs recurrent harness flaws across evaluated benchmarks, rather than restoring a specific external effect.

title: When Tools Fail: Benchmarking Dynamic Replanning and Anomaly Recovery in LLM Agents
why: ToolMaze tests explicit or implicit transient or permanent tool perturbations.

title: DelAct: A Replayable Boundary Runtime for Auditable and Governed LLM Agent Workflows
why: Separates deliberation actuation and append-only logging for replay idempotent execution and compensation.
note: IEEE/ACM IWQoS 2026; demonstrated in a ticket/invoice workflow under selected faults, not universal rollback.

title: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators for Reliable Tool-Augmented Large Language Model Systems
why: Classifies tool and orchestration failures, selects corrective actions under limited budgets and verifies reconstructed tool-using agent outcomes.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; controlled 100-task fault-injection evaluation and small model-in-loop tool study, not broadly reproduced production evidence.

title: TraceFix: Repairing Agent Coordination Protocols with TLA+ Counterexamples
why: Repairs LLM-generated multi-agent coordination protocols using TLA+ counterexamples and enforces topology conformance at runtime.
note: ACM CAIS 2026 peer-reviewed; TLC checks bounded modeled protocol safety, not fidelity of model to deployed actions or universal liveness and external side effects.

title: VerifyMAS: Hypothesis Verification for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
why: Verifies trajectory-level fault hypotheses before assigning agents and error categories across long multi-agent interactions.
note: 2026 preprint; Aegis-Bench and Who-and-When attribution results are author-reported. Verification concerns diagnosis hypotheses, not remote task-state correctness.

title: AgentForesight: Online Auditing for Early Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems
why: Learns prefix-only continue-or-alarm decisions to detect decisive multi-agent errors before downstream propagation.
note: 2026 preprint; AFTraj-2K results rely on curated safe traces and judge-consensus error boundaries. Early alarms are not evidence of repaired completion.

title: Debugging the Debuggers: Failure-Anchored Structured Recovery for Software Engineering Agents
why: PROBE gates recovery guidance on structured telemetry and grounded diagnosis for subsequent repair attempts.
note: ASE 2026 paper; 257 initially unresolved cases and outcomes reported by authors; diagnosis does not itself guarantee recovery.

title: Robust Agent Compensation (RAC): Teaching AI Agents to Compensate
why: Studies log-based compensation layers that track agent effects and support corrective execution.
note: 2026 preprint; claims are evaluated in selected framework and benchmark environments, not arbitrary APIs.

title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
why: Uses OS-effect inspection to make agent sandbox checkpointing more selective.

title: Rethinking Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark and Evaluation
why: Evaluates multiple plausible failure attributions instead of forcing one deterministic agent-step root cause.
note: 2026 preprint; MP-Bench studies ambiguity in failure attribution. Attribution agreement is not verified environment recovery.

title: ACRFence: Preventing Semantic Rollback Attacks in Agent Checkpoint-Restore
why: Addresses semantically different tool requests after checkpoint restoration that can replay effects or resurrect expired authority.
note: 2026 preprint; proof-of-concept and proposed replay-or-fork mitigation; no blanket protection across external providers.

title: AgentTrace: Causal Graph Tracing for Root Cause Analysis in Deployed Multi-Agent Systems
why: Reconstructs backward causal graphs from multi-agent execution logs and ranks root causes without LLM inference during diagnosis.
note: ICLR 2026 Agents in the Wild workshop paper; sub-second fault localization is author-reported on designed failure scenarios, not completed repair.

title: Wink: Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents
why: Monitors coding-agent drift, loops and tool failures and applies targeted runtime course-correction interventions.
note: 2026 preprint; author-reported production trajectory and intervention study; not general environment rollback.

title: Atomix: Timely, Transactional Tool Use for Reliable Agentic Workflows
why: Uses progress-aware resource frontiers to gate commits and distinguish bufferable reversible and irreversible effects.
note: Preprint; requires orchestrator/tool adapters. Authors do not claim distributed deployment or fully validated crash-safe exactly-once.

title: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
why: Studies robustness and repeated agent reliability under controlled stress.

title: DoVer: Intervention-Driven Auto Debugging for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
why: Verifies debugging hypotheses by actively intervening in multi-agent tasks.
note: 2025 arXiv version later revised in 2026.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
why: Introduces MAST taxonomy and MAST-Data of 1600-plus annotated multi-agent traces to distinguish design misalignment and verification failures.
note: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track; 14 failure modes from 150 manually studied traces. Diagnosis taxonomy informs intervention but does not directly recover committed state.

title: Where LLM Agents Fail and How They can Learn From Failures
why: Introduces AgentErrorTaxonomy and AgentErrorBench with root-cause targeted debugging feedback and iterative reruns.
